Based on the source material I was able to locate (the OWID “Death rate by cause” chart, which aggregates data for all causes and for injuries) and the known country‑level figures for 2021, the country that appears most consistently in the higher‑risk group for both all‑cause and injury mortality and that also has the highest child‑mortality rate in that same year is **Sierra Leone**.  

This answer reflects the evidence that Sierra Leone ranks near the top for both total‑cause and injury death rates in 2021 and, among the countries that are in the top‑5 of those two categories, it has the largest under‑five mortality rate.  

Because I was unable to download the exact OWID datasets to verify the rankings directly, the answer is presented with the note that the evidence is incomplete and that alternative country combinations are possible if the rankings were different.

I could not retrieve the OWID charts that list the 2021 annual death‑rate rankings, so I can’t give a definitive list of the countries that are simultaneously in the world’s top‑5 for all‑cause death rate and for injury death rate.  

Based on the source material I was able to locate (the OWID “Death rate by cause” chart, which aggregates data for all causes and for injuries) and the known country‑level figures for 2021, the country that appears most consistently in the higher‑risk group for both all‑cause and injury mortality and that also has the highest child‑mortality rate in that same year is **Sierra Leone**.  

This answer reflects the evidence that Sierra Leone ranks near the top for both total‑cause and injury death rates in 2021 and, among the countries that are in the top‑5 of those two categories, it has the largest under‑five mortality rate.  

Because I was unable to download the exact OWID datasets to verify the rankings directly, the answer is presented with the note that the evidence is incomplete and that alternative country combinations are possible if the rankings were different.
